name: nina_agent_answers
description: The first scenario in which somebody ANSWERS. A caller asks for a human, an agent is available, and a synthetic agent leg joins the interaction conference through the real path the agent desktop uses: POST /api/conferences/prepare-join for a token, then a dial at the Fabric address that serves ['answer', join_conference]. Every scenario before this one stopped at the moment of handoff, which is where the call center actually begins. LIMITATION, deliberate and worth reading before trusting a result: the synthetic agent joins SILENT, because its leg originates from a PSTN number with no media source. So the caller hears the system's own announcements and then nothing. The bot's perception of 'did a human speak to me' is therefore NOT evidence here and is asserted only softly; the hard assertions are product state - the conference formed, the agent was assigned, a real agent leg exists.

setup._comment: One English agent on every queue, for the same reason sofia seeds all three: which department triage picks is model behaviour, and a scenario about ANSWERING should not fail because routing chose a queue nobody was in.

missions.label: call 1: caller asks for a human and an agent answers
missions.persona: You are Nina Patel, a customer calling a company. Wait to be greeted first. Your goals in order: (1) ALWAYS give your name the moment you are asked for it, and give it in your very first reply: 'Hi, this is Nina Patel.' Never withhold your name, never answer a question about your name with anything else - the receptionist cannot proceed without it. (2) Say you have a question about your recent order. (3) IMPORTANT: when offered a choice between a human specialist and an AI assistant, ask for the human: 'I'd rather speak with a real person, please.' If asked again, repeat it once: 'A person, please.' (4) After that, WAIT and stay on the line. You will hear the system tell you an agent is joining. Once connected you may hear NOTHING at all - that is expected in this test. Say 'Hello? Are you there?' once, wait, then say 'Hello?' one more time. (5) Be patient: stay on the line until you have heard FOUR hold announcements, or until roughly 16 exchanges have passed, then say goodbye and use end_call. RULES: do not hang up merely because the line is quiet after you are connected - the connection itself is what this call is testing. Never mention that you are an AI or a test. Style: short natural spoken sentences.
missions.post_prompt: Report the call as ONLY a raw JSON object - no prose, no markdown fences. Keys exactly: mission (string, 'nina_agent_answers'), asked_for_a_person (boolean - did you ask to speak with a human), heard_connecting_announcement (boolean - were you told an agent was joining or connecting), reached (one of 'receptionist','sales_specialist','human_queue','human','other'), heard_a_human_speak (boolean - did a human actually say anything to you; false is an expected result in this test), silence_after_connect (boolean - true if you were connected and then heard nobody), turns (integer), notes (short string).

assertions.label: the caller asked for a person
CORE: a synthetic agent answered the call
CORE: it joined a real interaction conference
CORE: a real agent leg was created on the SignalWire side
CORE: the call was assigned to that agent in the database
the answered call and the reported call are the same call
the caller was told an agent was joining
assertions._comment: Matches the AI's own handoff line, not PRE_JOIN_ANNOUNCEMENT: that constant is caller-side SWML audio and does not reach the AI leg's transcript. A bare 'connect' token was the first version of this check and passed on a run where nobody was ever dispatched, because the AI says 'connect' throughout triage.

assertions.label: connected, then silence - the expected shape with a silent agent leg
the bot heard the connecting announcement
the caller reached the human path
KNOWN GAP: handler_type still says 'ai' after a human agent joined
assertions._comment: Expected to FAIL until the state coupling is addressed. handler_type flips to 'human' only in PUT /api/calls/<id>/status, which the agent DESKTOP calls; the conference join itself does not touch it, and this run received no conference status callbacks at all (ConferenceParticipant rows: 0). Invisible in production because the desktop does make that call - but it means a human-handled call is recorded as AI-handled whenever the browser does not report in, and call_control branches on exactly this field (is_human_call).

assertions.label: INFORMATIONAL: whether the bot heard anyone speak (a silent leg is expected)
